definitions.gloss: beat; the basic unit of musical time; counter for beats
definitions.explanation: The regular pulse that underlies a piece of music, and the counter used to count those pulses. In Japanese music theory it is the traditional term for the English 'beat.'

examples.japanese: {指揮者|しきしゃ}が{拍|はく}を{取|と}る。
{曲|きょく}の{拍|はく}に{合|あ}わせて{手|て}をたたく。
examples.english: I clap along to the beat of the song.

examples.japanese: {音楽|おんがく}の{拍|はく}を{正確|せいかく}に{刻|きざ}むのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Keeping the beat of music precisely is difficult.

notes:
The traditional term in Japanese music theory for a beat — the basic pulse of music — and the counter for counting beats (e.g. {二|に}{拍|はく}, two beats). In casual and pop-music contexts the loanword ビート is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拍|はく}を{取|と}る: to keep the beat
- {拍|はく}に{合|あ}わせる: to match the beat
- {表|おもて}{拍|はく}: the on-beat
- {裏|うら}{拍|はく}: the off-beat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {拍子|びょうし}: time; meter — how beats are grouped (e.g. {三|さん}{拍子|びょうし}, triple time)
- ビート: beat — the everyday loanword, common in pop and rock
